newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New chief seen boosting Ansett revival hopes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New chief seen boosting Ansett revival hopes.

text.p: The appointment of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd's managing director Rod Eddington as the new executive chairman of Ansett Australia has boosted hopes of a revival for the loss-making Australian airline, analysts said.

"Cathay Pacific has been a very successful airline under his leadership and he's had a lot of experience in Asia which is where Ansett International is focused," one Sydney aviation analyst said. "It has to be seen as a positive," he said.
News Corp Ltd unit News Ltd, which owns half of Ansett, announced late on Friday that Eddington would take up the position from Janauary 1997, ending months of speculation about the move.

"Rod's appointment marks the culmination of extensive negotiations, a lengthy and considered process befitting one of the industry's finest executives," News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley said in a statement.
Cowley was also Ansett's executive charman until Eddington's appointment. He said he would stay on as an Ansett director.
"I had always planned to relinquish my role as executive chairman once a suitably talented aviation manager was secured for News," Cowley said.

Eddington's appointment delighted aviation analysts, who have been privately critical of Cowley's performance at Ansett, which has relinquished domestic market dominance to its newly-privatised rival Qantas Airways Ltd in the last two years.
Ansett's profits have also dived in tandem with its market share and in the year to June 30, 1996 it made a pre-tax and abnormals loss.

The analysts said Eddington was much better placed to revive Ansett than Cowley, who is not seen as an airline man. Analysts also welcomed the resolution of what had been an unsettling two-year long shake-up of Ansett's ownership and management.

"Eddington's got a very good track record ...", one analyst said. Eddington's appointment came on the same day as final shareholder approval for Air New Zealand Ltd's purchase of TNT Ltd's 50 percent stake in Ansett, a process which has dragged on since mid-1995.
The terms of the deal were announced earlier this month, with Air New Zealand paying TNT A$325 million (US257 million) and agreeing to invest a further A$150 million in Ansett.
News also agreed to invest A$50 million in Ansett to help fund the rejuvenation of its fleet, which has struggled to compete with Qantas' newer and bigger planes.
Eddington said in his statement of appointment that Ansett welcomed a welcome a new partner in Air New Zealand."

"Together we will create new synergies and additional opportunities for growth," he said. "And I look forward to working with the Ansett Australia team in the confidence we will achieve our goals: to increase revenues, reduce costs and retain the enviable reputation for high safety standards and customer service of which Ansett is so justifiably proud."
Analysts said Eddington was likely to focus first on cutting costs. Cowley said last month Ansett had to cut A$150 million a year from costs.
